    SAP Models¶

    Pydantic models of the SAP business objects that the SAP class reads and changes - see Models for their naming and usage.

    sap_models ¶

    Pydantic models for the SAP S/4HANA OData APIs used by the SAP class (see sap.py).

    The module contains: * Field types and helpers for SAP / OData formats (e.g. OData V2 "/Date(...)/" dates, SAP flags "X" / "", fixed-length item numbers). * Base classes: SAPODataModel (all SAP entity models) and SAPODataCreateModel (models that are converted into the payload of a deep insert / deep create). * Models describing OData services, their availability and SAP error responses. * Create models (e.g. SAPMaintenanceOrderModel) - validated input data that is converted into the OData payload with to_odata(). * Response models (e.g. SAPMaintenanceOrderResponseModel) - typed results of read requests. * Query models (e.g. SAPMaintenanceOrderQueryModel) - search criteria of the list methods.

    Class hierarchy - the subclasses mostly declare fields, the behavior comes from the base classes:

    SAPODataModel                     parse SAP responses, str() = compact JSON
├── *ResponseModel                results of SAP.get_*() / iter_*()
└── SAPODataCreateModel           to_odata() / to_odata_update()
    ├── *Model                    data of SAP.create_*(), changes of SAP.update_*()
    ├── SAPPurchasingItemModel    common fields of purchasing document items
    ├── SAPSourcingItemModel      common fields of RFQ and quotation items
    └── SAPSourcingDocumentModel  common fields of RFQ and quotation headers
SAPODataQueryModel                to_odata() = $filter / $orderby / $expand
└── *QueryModel                   search criteria of SAP.get_*s() / iter_*s()

    A comment above each subclass names what it inherits and which SAP methods use it. These notes are comments on purpose: pydantic puts the class docstring into the JSON schema ("description"), and LLM tools that take or return the models show it to the LLM - so docstrings describe the data for API users and LLMs, comments explain the code to developers.

    The Python attribute names of the models are snake case, the aliases are the OData property names of the SAP APIs. Both can be used to initialize the models.

    See sap.py for the documentation of the SAP APIs and how to activate them.

    Classes:

    Name Description
    SAPBusinessObjectType

    An SAP business object type (BOR object type, transaction SWO1) with the structure of its key.
    SAPODataModel

    Base class of all models for SAP OData entities.
    SAPODataCreateModel

    Base class of the models used to create SAP documents (deep insert / deep create).
    SAPPurchasingItemModel

    Base class of the items of purchasing documents (purchase order, contract and requisition).
    ODataCondition

    Describes how a field of a query model becomes a condition of the OData $filter.
    ODataDeletionCondition

    Describes the condition of a deletion filter (is_marked_for_deletion of the query models).
    ODataTextSearch

    Describes how the name / description criterion of a query model is resolved via a text entity set.
    SAPODataQueryModel

    Base class of the search criteria for SAP OData collections (list and iterator methods).
    SAPODataTextResponseModel

    An entity of a text entity set as returned by SAP - all properties are kept (see ODataTextSearch).
    SAPODataTextQueryModel

    Query of the keys of a text or item entity set (see SAP._resolve_text_search() and SAP._find_keys_via_items()).
    SAPODataServiceModel

    Definition of an SAP OData service (API) used by this module.
    SAPODataServiceState

    Possible results of an OData service availability check.
    SAPODataServiceStatusModel

    Result of the availability check for one SAP OData service.
    SAPAuthCheckState

    Possible results of an authentication / principal propagation health check.
    SAPAuthCheckStatusModel

    Result of a single step of an authentication / principal propagation health check.
    SAPODataErrorDetailModel

    A single detail message of an SAP OData error response.
    SAPODataErrorModel

    An error returned by an SAP OData service.
    SAPMaintenanceOrderComponentModel

    A component (material, e.g. a spare part) of an operation of a maintenance order (API_MAINTENANCEORDER).
    SAPTaskListReferenceModel

    A maintenance task list whose operations and materials are taken over into a new maintenance order.
    SAPMaintenanceOrderOperationModel

    An operation of an SAP Plant Maintenance order (API_MAINTENANCEORDER).
    SAPMaintenanceOrderModel

    Data to create an SAP Plant Maintenance order (API_MAINTENANCEORDER).
    SAPMaintenanceOrderComponentResponseModel

    A component (material) of a maintenance order operation as returned by SAP (API_MAINTENANCEORDER).
    SAPMaintenanceOrderOperationResponseModel

    An operation of an SAP Plant Maintenance order as returned by SAP (API_MAINTENANCEORDER).
    SAPMaintenanceOrderObjectListItemResponseModel

    An entry of the object list of a maintenance order as returned by SAP (API_MAINTENANCEORDER).
    SAPMaintenanceOrderResponseModel

    An SAP Plant Maintenance order as returned by SAP (API_MAINTENANCEORDER).
    SAPMaintenanceOrderQueryModel

    Search criteria for SAP maintenance orders (API_MAINTENANCEORDER).
    SAPMaintenanceNotificationItemModel

    An item (damage / object part) of an SAP maintenance notification (API_MAINTNOTIFICATION).
    SAPMaintenanceNotificationModel

    Data to create an SAP maintenance notification (API_MAINTNOTIFICATION, OData V2).
    SAPMaintenanceNotificationItemResponseModel

    An item of an SAP maintenance notification as returned by SAP (API_MAINTNOTIFICATION).
    SAPMaintenanceNotificationResponseModel

    SAPMaintenanceNotificationQueryModel

    SAPBusinessObjectType dataclass ¶

    SAPBusinessObjectType(
    label: str,
    key_lengths: tuple[int, ...] = (),
    bo_type: str = "",
)

    An SAP business object type (BOR object type, transaction SWO1) with the structure of its key.

    Use SAPBusinessObjectType.get() to look up a type by its code (see SAP_BUSINESS_OBJECT_TYPES).

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    label str

    Name of the business object, e.g. "maintenance order".
    key_lengths tuple[int, ...]

    Lengths of the key fields in SAP's internal format, e.g. (10, 4) for a material document (document number and year). Empty if the key structure is unknown.
    bo_type str

    The code of the type, e.g. "BUS2017" - set by get().

    Methods:

    Name Description
    get

    Get an SAP business object type by its code.
    get_key_fields

    Convert the business object ID of a reference (e.g. a business workspace) into the key fields of the SAP object.
    get_business_object_id

    Convert the key fields of an SAP object into the business object ID of a reference (e.g. a business workspace).

    get classmethod ¶

    get(bo_type: str) -> SAPBusinessObjectType

    Get an SAP business object type by its code.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    bo_type str

    The SAP business object type, e.g. "BUS2017" (see SAP_BUSINESS_OBJECT_TYPES).

    		 required

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    SAPBusinessObjectType SAPBusinessObjectType

    The type or - for types that are not in SAP_BUSINESS_OBJECT_TYPES - a generic "object" type with unknown key structure.

    def get_key_fields(self, bo_id: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Convert the business object ID of a reference (e.g. a business workspace) into the key fields of the SAP object.

    Business object references store the key in SAP's internal format: key fields with leading
    zeros, concatenated for composite keys (e.g. "49000001232026" for material document 4900000123
    of 2026). The OData APIs expect the key fields in the external format.

    Args:
        bo_id (str):
            The business object ID, e.g. "49000001232026".

    Returns:
        tuple[str, ...]:
            The key fields in SAP's external format (ALPHA conversion: numeric keys without leading
            zeros), e.g. ("4000340",) or ("4900000123", "2026"). IDs of types with unknown key
            structure are not split.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            If the ID does not have the length of the composite key of the type.

    """

    bo_id = bo_id.strip()
    lengths = self.key_lengths or (len(bo_id),)
    if len(lengths) == 1:
        parts = [bo_id]
    elif len(bo_id) == sum(lengths):
        offsets = [sum(lengths[:index]) for index in range(len(lengths))]
        parts = [bo_id[offset : offset + length].strip() for offset, length in zip(offsets, lengths, strict=True)]
    else:
        message = "Unexpected ID -> '{}' of SAP business object type -> '{}'.".format(bo_id, self.bo_type)
        raise ValueError(message)

    return tuple((part.lstrip("0") or "0") if part.isdigit() else part for part in parts)

    def get_business_object_id(self, key_fields: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
    """Convert the key fields of an SAP object into the business object ID of a reference (e.g. a business workspace).

    The reverse of get_key_fields(): numeric key fields get their leading zeros, composite
    keys are concatenated, e.g. ("4900000123", "2026") -> "49000001232026" for a material document.

    Args:
        key_fields (tuple[str, ...]):
            The key fields in SAP's external format, e.g. ("413",).

    Returns:
        str:
            The business object ID in SAP's internal format, e.g. "0000000413".

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            If the key structure of the type is unknown or the key fields don't match it.

    """

    if len(key_fields) != len(self.key_lengths):
        message = "Key fields -> {} don't match SAP business object type -> '{}'.".format(key_fields, self.bo_type)
        raise ValueError(message)

    parts = []
    for field, length in zip(key_fields, self.key_lengths, strict=True):
        field = str(field).strip()
        if len(field) > length:
            message = "Key field -> '{}' is longer than {} characters.".format(field, length)
            raise ValueError(message)
        # Numeric fields with leading zeros (ALPHA conversion), others filled up with blanks:
        parts.append(field.zfill(length) if field.isdigit() else field.ljust(length))

    # References store the ID without trailing blanks (e.g. equipment 'P-3000-N001'):
    return "".join(parts).rstrip()

    SAPODataModel ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Base class of all models for SAP OData entities.

    The Python attribute names are snake case. The aliases are the OData property names of the SAP API. Both can be used to initialize the models. Default values are validated as well (e.g. item numbers are padded to their SAP length).

    OData properties that are not modelled are ignored in the response models: SAP returns many technical properties (often in raw OData formats like "/Date(...)/") that would only be noise for users or LLMs. Model a property to return it. The create models reject them instead (see SAPODataCreateModel).

    Direct subclasses are the response models (*ResponseModel) that the SAP read methods validate the OData results with (model_validate()), e.g. SAP.get_sales_order().

    @model_validator(mode="before")
@classmethod
def drop_odata_annotations(cls, data: object) -> object:
    """Drop OData protocol annotations that carry no business data.

    These are "__metadata" (OData V2), "@odata.context" / "@odata.etag" (OData V4)
    and navigation properties that have not been expanded ({"__deferred": ...}).
    Otherwise the create models would reject them as unknown fields - e.g. in an
    entity read from SAP and passed to a create or update.

    """

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return data

    return {
        key: value
        for key, value in data.items()
        if not key.startswith(("__", "@")) and not (isinstance(value, dict) and "__deferred" in value)
    }

    @model_validator(mode="before")
@classmethod
def drop_empty_text_lists(cls, data: object) -> object:
    """Treat an empty text sent for a list field as omitted.

    LLMs sometimes send "" instead of [] for lists they don't need - e.g.
    "to_SuplrInvcItemMaterial": "" for a supplier invoice with purchase order items
    only. The validation would fail and the tool call would have to be repeated.

    Args:
        data (object):
            The input data of the model (a dict with OData or field names).

    Returns:
        object:
            The data without the list fields that are "" - other values are unchanged.

    """

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return data

    list_keys = {
        key
        for name, field in cls.model_fields.items()
        if get_origin(field.annotation) is list
        or any(get_origin(arg) is list for arg in get_args(field.annotation))
        for key in (name, field.alias)
        if key
    }

    return {key: value for key, value in data.items() if not (value == "" and key in list_keys)}

    SAPODataCreateModel ¶

    Bases: SAPODataModel

    Base class of the models used to create SAP documents (deep insert / deep create).

    Serialization uses the OData property names (aliases), so to_odata() returns the payload as expected by the SAP API. Only the modelled fields can be set - unknown fields are rejected, so an LLM can't invent OData properties that SAP rejects only after the user has confirmed the create or update. Model a property to make it settable.

    The subclasses (e.g. SAPSalesOrderModel and its SAPSalesOrderItemModel) only declare the fields with their validations and inherit: * to_odata(): the payload of the SAP create methods, e.g. SAP.create_sales_order(). * to_odata_update(): validates the changes of the SAP update methods, e.g. SAP.update_sales_order(), with the same field definitions as a create. * check_unknown_fields(): rejects unknown field names (e.g. invented by an LLM).

    @model_validator(mode="before")
@classmethod
def check_unknown_fields(cls, data: object) -> object:
    """Reject all fields that are not modelled - with their attribute or OData name.

    Unknown fields are misspelled or invented names (e.g. "WrntyRepairDate" instead of
    "WrntyClaimRepairDate") or navigation properties ("_...") copied from a read. SAP would
    reject them - only after the user confirmed the create.

    """

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return data

    known = set(cls.model_fields) | {field.alias for field in cls.model_fields.values() if field.alias}
    unknown = sorted(key for key in data if key not in known)
    if unknown:
        message = "Unknown field(s) -> {} for {} - only its modelled fields can be set".format(
            unknown, cls.__name__
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return data

    @classmethod
def to_odata_update(cls, changes: dict) -> dict:
    """Return the OData payload to update (PATCH) individual fields of an existing document.

    Each changed value is validated and serialized with the definition of the
    corresponding field of this model (type, length, upper case, SAP / OData
    formats) - so updates get the same treatment as creates. Validations that
    span several fields (e.g. "end date after start date") are not applied, as
    the other fields of the document are not known.

    Args:
        changes (dict):
            The fields to change - with snake case attribute names or OData
            property names, e.g. {"description": "New text"} or
            {"MaintenanceOrderDesc": "New text"}. Fields that are not modelled
            are rejected.

    Returns:
        dict:
            The payload with OData property names.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            If a field is unknown, cannot be changed (READ_ONLY_PROPERTIES), refers to
            child entities (e.g. items) or has an invalid value (pydantic.ValidationError
            is a ValueError).

    Example:
        >>> SAPSalesOrderModel.to_odata_update({"requested_delivery_date": "2026-12-01"})
        {'RequestedDeliveryDate': '/Date(1796083200000)/'}

    """

    fields = {}
    for name, field in cls.model_fields.items():
        fields[name] = field
        if field.alias:
            fields[field.alias] = field

    payload = {}
    for key, value in changes.items():
        field = fields.get(key)
        odata_name = field.alias or key if field else key
        if odata_name in cls.READ_ONLY_PROPERTIES:
            message = "Field -> '{}' cannot be changed - {}".format(key, cls.READ_ONLY_PROPERTIES[odata_name])
            raise ValueError(message)
        if field is None:
            message = "Unknown field -> '{}' for {} - only its modelled fields can be changed".format(
                key, cls.__name__
            )
            raise ValueError(message)
        if get_origin(field.annotation) is list or any(
            get_origin(argument) is list for argument in get_args(field.annotation)
        ):
            message = "Field -> '{}' refers to child entities which cannot be changed with an update".format(key)
            raise ValueError(message)
        adapter = TypeAdapter(field.rebuild_annotation())
        try:
            validated = adapter.validate_python(value)
        except ValidationError:
            # Agents often send numbers for texts (e.g. a year or a code) - accept them as text:
            if not isinstance(value, int | float | Decimal) or isinstance(value, bool):
                raise
            validated = adapter.validate_python(format(value, "f") if isinstance(value, Decimal) else str(value))
        payload[field.alias or key] = adapter.dump_python(validated, mode="json")

    return payload

    Base class of the items of purchasing documents (purchase order, contract and requisition).

    Provides the fields and validations common to all purchasing document items. The subclasses (SAPPurchaseOrderItemModel, SAPPurchaseContractItemModel and SAPPurchaseRequisitionItemModel) add the item specific fields (e.g. the short text, whose OData name differs per document type).

    Contract with the subclasses (the validations access these fields by name): * item (required): the item number - used in error messages. * text (required): the short text - without it, a material is always required. * account_assignments (optional): the account assignments - items without this field (e.g. purchase contract items) skip the account assignment check. * purchase_contract / purchase_contract_item and purchase_requisition / purchase_requisition_item (optional): the item of another document the item refers to - SAP copies material, text, material group and plant from it, so such an item needs neither a material nor a text.

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_material_or_text(self) -> Self:
    """Validate that the item has a material, a short text plus a material group or a reference item."""

    # SAP copies material, text and material group from the contract or requisition item the item refers to
    # (verified in S/4HANA 2023 for purchase orders):
    refers_to_item = (
        getattr(self, "purchase_contract", None) and getattr(self, "purchase_contract_item", None)
    ) or (getattr(self, "purchase_requisition", None) and getattr(self, "purchase_requisition_item", None))
    if not self.material and not (getattr(self, "text", None) and self.material_group) and not refers_to_item:
        message = (
            "Item -> {} needs a material, a text plus a material group, or the purchase contract or requisition "
            "item it refers to".format(getattr(self, "item", "?"))
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    def to_filter(self, value: object, odata_version: int) -> str:
    """Return the $filter condition for a field value.

    Args:
        value (object):
            The (not empty) value of the query model field.
        odata_version (int):
            The OData version of the service (2 or 4).

    Returns:
        str:
            The condition, e.g. "(MaintenanceOrderType eq 'YA01' or MaintenanceOrderType eq 'YA02')".

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            If a condition on child entities is used with an OData V2 service.

    """

    prefix = "i/" if self.path else ""

    def literal(single_value: object) -> str:
        return odata_literal(
            self.values.get(single_value, single_value) if self.values else single_value,
            odata_version=odata_version,
            kind=self.kind,
        )

    def condition(single_value: object) -> str:
        name = prefix + self.property if isinstance(self.property, str) else ""
        match self.operator:
            case "contains":
                if odata_version == 2:
                    return "substringof({}, {})".format(literal(single_value), name)
                return "contains({}, {})".format(name, literal(single_value))
            case "valid_on":
                start, end = (prefix + name for name in self.property)
                return "{} le {} and {} ge {}".format(start, literal(single_value), end, literal(single_value))
            case "le" if self.kind == "timestamp" and not isinstance(single_value, datetime):
                # A date as upper limit of a timestamp includes the whole day:
                return "{} lt {}".format(name, literal(single_value + timedelta(days=1)))
            case _:
                return "{} {} {}".format(name, self.operator, literal(single_value))

    values = value if isinstance(value, list) else [value]
    result = " or ".join(condition(single_value) for single_value in values)
    if len(values) > 1:
        result = "({})".format(result)

    if self.path:
        if odata_version != 4:
            message = "Conditions on child entities ('{}') are only supported by OData V4 services".format(
                self.path
            )
            raise ValueError(message)
        result = "{}/any(i:{})".format(self.path, result)

    return result

    Describes the condition of a deletion filter (is_marked_for_deletion of the query models).

    The field value True selects the deleted objects (property eq deleted_value), False the objects that are not deleted (property ne deleted_value). With a path, the deletion indicator is on the items: a document is deleted if all its items are deleted (e.g. purchase orders - SAP doesn't set the header indicator when all items are deleted).

    def to_filter(self, value: object, odata_version: int) -> str:
    """Return the $filter condition for the value of the deletion filter.

    Args:
        value (object):
            True for the deleted objects, False for the objects that are not deleted.
        odata_version (int):
            The OData version of the service (2 or 4).

    Returns:
        str:
            The condition, e.g. "EquipmentIsMarkedForDeletion ne true" or
            "_PurchaseOrderItem/any(i:i/PurchasingDocumentDeletionCode ne 'L')".

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            If a condition on child entities is used with an OData V2 service.

    """

    literal = odata_literal(self.deleted_value, odata_version=odata_version, kind=self.kind)
    if not self.path:
        return "{} {} {}".format(self.property, "eq" if value else "ne", literal)

    if odata_version != 4:
        message = "Conditions on child entities ('{}') are only supported by OData V4 services".format(self.path)
        raise ValueError(message)
    if value:
        return "{}/all(i:i/{} eq {})".format(self.path, self.property, literal)
    return "{}/any(i:i/{} ne {})".format(self.path, self.property, literal)

    SAPODataQueryModel ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Base class of the search criteria for SAP OData collections (list and iterator methods).

    The fields of the subclasses are the search criteria. Fields with an ODataCondition in their metadata become conditions of the OData $filter (all conditions must match); fields that are None (or empty lists) are ignored. The subclasses define: * sort_by: the sort criteria, mapped to the $orderby expression with SORT_PROPERTIES. * expand_items (optional): whether to read the child entities (with EXPAND). * BASE_CONDITIONS (optional): conditions that are always part of the filter.

    The subclasses (*QueryModel) inherit limit, sort_direction, page_size and to_odata(). They are the query parameter of the SAP list methods, e.g. SAP.get_sales_orders(), which pass to_odata() to SAP._iter_odata_collection(). Their JSON schema serves as the parameters of LLM tools as well - so callers give readable criteria, not OData expressions.

    def to_odata(self, odata_version: int) -> dict:
    """Return the OData query options ($filter, $orderby, $expand) of the search criteria.

    The limit and the page size are not included - they control the paging (see
    SAP._iter_odata_collection()).

    Args:
        odata_version (int):
            The OData version of the service (2 or 4).

    Returns:
        dict:
            The query options, e.g. {"$filter": "MaintenancePlanningPlant eq '1010'",
            "$orderby": "MaintenanceOrder desc"}.

    """

    conditions = list(self.BASE_CONDITIONS) + self.to_odata_conditions(odata_version=odata_version)

    sort_by = getattr(self, "sort_by", None)
    params = {"$orderby": self.SORT_PROPERTIES[sort_by].format(direction=self.sort_direction)} if sort_by else {}
    if conditions:
        params["$filter"] = " and ".join(
            "({})".format(condition) if " or " in condition and not condition.startswith("(") else condition
            for condition in conditions
        )
    if self.EXPAND and getattr(self, "expand_items", False):
        params["$expand"] = self.EXPAND

    return params

    def to_odata_conditions(self, odata_version: int, navigation: str = "", exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> list[str]:
    """Return the $filter conditions of the fields with an ODataCondition (without BASE_CONDITIONS).

    With a navigation property, the conditions refer to the entity it leads to - so another entity set
    can be filtered by the criteria of this query, e.g. material document items by the posting date of
    their header ("to_MaterialDocumentHeader/PostingDate ge ..."). OData V2 supports this for to-one
    navigation properties only. Conditions on child entities (ODataCondition.path) are left out then.

    Args:
        odata_version (int):
            The OData version of the service (2 or 4).
        navigation (str, optional):
            The to-one navigation property to the entity of this query, e.g. "to_MaterialDocumentHeader".
            Defaults to "" (conditions on the entity itself).
        exclude (tuple[str, ...], optional):
            Fields to leave out, e.g. criteria that the other query already has. Defaults to ().

    Returns:
        list[str]:
            The conditions, e.g. ["MaterialDocumentYear eq '2026'", "PostingDate ge datetime'...'"].

    """

    conditions = []
    for name, field in type(self).model_fields.items():
        marker = next((item for item in field.metadata if isinstance(item, ODataCondition)), None)
        value = getattr(self, name)
        if marker is None or value is None or value == [] or name in exclude:
            continue
        if navigation:
            if marker.path:
                continue
            prefixed = (
                "{}/{}".format(navigation, marker.property)
                if isinstance(marker.property, str)
                else tuple("{}/{}".format(navigation, part) for part in marker.property)
            )
            marker = replace(marker, property=prefixed)
        conditions.append(marker.to_filter(value=value, odata_version=odata_version))

    return conditions

    def to_odata(self, odata_version: int) -> dict:  # noqa: ARG002
    """Return the OData query options of the text query.

    Args:
        odata_version (int):
            The OData version of the service (not needed - the conditions are given as expressions).

    Returns:
        dict:
            The query options ($filter, $orderby, $select).

    """

    params = {}
    # Joined conditions are parenthesized - each one can have a top-level 'or' (e.g. one per text property):
    if len(self.conditions) == 1:
        params["$filter"] = self.conditions[0]
    elif self.conditions:
        params["$filter"] = " and ".join("({})".format(condition) for condition in self.conditions)
    if self.order_by:
        params["$orderby"] = self.order_by
    if self.select:
        params["$select"] = self.select

    return params

    @classmethod
def from_response(cls, response: requests.Response) -> Self:
    """Build an SAPODataErrorModel from a (failed) HTTP response.

    This method never raises an exception - if the response cannot be
    interpreted, the raw response text is preserved instead.

    Args:
        response (requests.Response):
            The failed HTTP response.

    Returns:
        SAPODataErrorModel:
            The parsed error.

    """

    error = cls(status_code=response.status_code, raw_text=response.text or "")

    try:
        error_body = response.json().get("error", {})
    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
        # Not JSON (e.g. HTML error page) - keep raw text only:
        content_type = (response.headers.get("content-type") or "").lower()
        error.message = "HTML error page returned" if "html" in content_type else (response.text or "")[:500]
        return error

    if not isinstance(error_body, dict):
        return error

    error.code = str(error_body.get("code", ""))
    message = error_body.get("message", "")
    # OData V2 wraps the message in a dict with language and value:
    error.message = message.get("value", "") if isinstance(message, dict) else str(message)

    # OData V2 provides details in "innererror.errordetails", OData V4 in "details":
    raw_details = error_body.get("details") or (error_body.get("innererror") or {}).get("errordetails") or []
    for raw_detail in raw_details:
        if not isinstance(raw_detail, dict):
            continue
        detail_message = raw_detail.get("message", "")
        error.details.append(
            SAPODataErrorDetailModel(
                code=str(raw_detail.get("code", "")),
                message=detail_message.get("value", "")
                if isinstance(detail_message, dict)
                else str(detail_message),
                severity=str(raw_detail.get("severity") or raw_detail.get("@Common.Severity") or ""),
                target=str(raw_detail.get("target") or raw_detail.get("propertyref") or ""),
            ),
        )

    return error

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_dates(self) -> Self:
    """Default the basic start date and validate that the basic end date is not before it."""

    # The API does not default the basic dates - without them SAP rejects the order with
    # IW/426 "Forward scheduling: Please enter start date". An end date alone is left
    # as is (backward scheduling):
    if self.basic_start_datetime is None and self.basic_end_datetime is None:
        self.basic_start_datetime = datetime.now(tz=UTC).replace(microsecond=0)

    # Compare as UTC timestamps (naive datetimes are treated as UTC, see serialize_odata_datetime()):
    start, end = (
        value.replace(tzinfo=value.tzinfo or UTC) if value else None
        for value in (self.basic_start_datetime, self.basic_end_datetime)
    )
    if start and end and end < start:
        message = "Basic end date -> {} is before basic start date -> {}".format(
            self.basic_end_datetime,
            self.basic_start_datetime,
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    def to_odata(self) -> dict:
    """Return the OData payload of the order (deep create of the order with its operations).

    The task list reference, the long text and the components of the operations are not part of it:
    SAP cannot include a task list with the API and rejects components in the deep
    create, nor is the long text - SAP.create_maintenance_order() handles them.

    Returns:
        dict:
            The payload with OData property names.

    """

    payload = super().to_odata()
    payload.pop("TaskListReference", None)
    payload.pop("MaintenanceOrderLongText", None)
    for operation in payload.get("to_MaintenanceOrderOperation", []):
        operation.pop("to_MaintOrderOpComponent_2", None)

    return payload

    def accepts(self, entity: BaseModel) -> bool:
    """Check the deletion flag - the API only has it in the status text, which SAP can't filter by (HTTP 501).

    Args:
        entity (BaseModel):
            The maintenance order read (SAPMaintenanceOrderResponseModel).

    Returns:
        bool:
            True if the order matches is_marked_for_deletion (or the criterion isn't set).

    """

    if self.is_marked_for_deletion is None:
        return True

    order = cast("SAPMaintenanceOrderResponseModel", entity)

    return ("DLFL" in (order.system_status or "").split()) == self.is_marked_for_deletion

def check_consistency(self) -> Self:
    """Validate dependencies between fields."""

    if self.technical_object and not self.technical_object_type:
        message = "Technical object -> '{}' needs a technical object type ('EAMS_EQUI' or 'EAMS_FL')".format(

    if self.required_start_date and self.required_end_date and self.required_end_date < self.required_start_date:
        message = "Required end date -> {} is before required start date -> {}".format(
            self.required_end_date,
            self.required_start_date,
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    Also match numeric equipment numbers with leading zeros.

    @field_validator("technical_object_ids")
@classmethod
def add_padded_equipment_numbers(cls, values: list[str] | None) -> list[str] | None:
    """Also match numeric equipment numbers with leading zeros.

    TechnicalObject is a generic field without ALPHA conversion: SAP stores a numeric
    equipment number with leading zeros ('000000000010000004'), so '10000004' alone
    finds nothing. The unpadded value is kept for numeric functional location labels.

    """

    if not values:
        return values

    return list(
        dict.fromkeys(
            padded
            for value in values
            for padded in (value, value.zfill(18) if value.isdigit() and len(value) < 18 else value)
        )
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_units(self) -> Self:
    """Fill in the order unit for the price, the schedule lines and the account assignments.

    OData V4 rejects quantities without their unit. The schedule lines must use the item's unit.

    """

    if self.price_unit is not None:
        self.price_unit_of_measure = self.price_unit_of_measure or self.unit
    for account_assignment in self.account_assignments:
        if account_assignment.quantity is not None:
            account_assignment.unit = account_assignment.unit or self.unit
    for schedule_line in self.schedule_lines:
        schedule_line.unit = schedule_line.unit or self.unit
        if schedule_line.unit != self.unit:
            message = "Schedule line -> {} has unit -> '{}' but the item -> {} has unit -> '{}'".format(
                schedule_line.schedule_line, schedule_line.unit, self.item, self.unit
            )
            raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_item_currencies(self) -> Self:
    """Fill in the purchase order's currency for the item prices (OData V4 needs the currency with the amount)."""

    for item in self.items:
        if item.net_price is not None:
            item.currency = item.currency or self.currency
            if not item.currency:
                message = (
                    "Item -> {} has a `net_price` but no currency - give the purchase order's `currency`".format(
                        item.item
                    )
                )
                raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    def to_odata(self, odata_version: int) -> dict:
    """Return the OData query options - with the items if the deletion flag is a criterion (see accepts()).

    SAP.iter_purchase_contracts() drops the items again if they haven't been requested (expand_items).

    Args:
        odata_version (int):
            The OData version of the service.

    Returns:
        dict:
            The query options ($filter, $orderby, $expand).

    """

    params = super().to_odata(odata_version=odata_version)
    if self.is_marked_for_deletion is not None:
        params["$expand"] = self.EXPAND

    return params

    def accepts(self, entity: BaseModel) -> bool:
    """Check the deletion flag - deleting a contract sets the indicator of its items, not of the header.

    The API (OData V2) can't filter by the items, so the contracts are checked when read.

    Args:
        entity (BaseModel):
            The purchase contract read with its items (SAPPurchaseContractResponseModel).

    Returns:
        bool:
            True if the contract matches is_marked_for_deletion (or the criterion isn't set).

    """

    if self.is_marked_for_deletion is None:
        return True

    contract = cast("SAPPurchaseContractResponseModel", entity)
    items = contract.items or []
    is_deleted = contract.deletion_code == "L" or bool(items and all(item.deletion_code == "L" for item in items))

    return is_deleted == self.is_marked_for_deletion

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_units_and_currency(self) -> Self:
    """Fill in the item's unit for the account assignments and check the currency of the price.

    OData V4 rejects quantities without their unit and amounts without their currency.

    """

    self.unit_iso_code = self.unit_iso_code or unit_iso_code(self.unit)
    if not self.unit_iso_code:
        message = (
            "Item -> {} needs a `unit_iso_code` - the ISO code of unit -> '{}' is not known".format(
                self.item, self.unit
            )
            if self.unit
            else "Item -> {} needs a `unit` or `unit_iso_code`".format(self.item)
        )
        raise ValueError(message)
    for account_assignment in self.account_assignments:
        if account_assignment.quantity is not None and not account_assignment.unit_iso_code:
            account_assignment.unit_iso_code = unit_iso_code(account_assignment.unit) or self.unit_iso_code
    if self.price is not None and not self.currency:
        message = "Item -> {} has a `price` but no `currency`".format(self.item)
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

def to_odata_update(cls, changes: dict) -> dict:
    """Return the OData payload to update individual fields of an item - a new unit as ISO code.

    Args:
        changes (dict):
            The fields to change (see SAPODataCreateModel.to_odata_update()).

    Returns:
        dict:
            The payload with OData property names.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            If a field is invalid or the ISO code of a new unit is not known.

    """

    payload = super().to_odata_update(changes)
    if "BaseUnit" in payload:
        unit = payload.pop("BaseUnit")
        payload.setdefault("BaseUnitISOCode", unit_iso_code(unit))
        if not payload["BaseUnitISOCode"]:
            message = "The ISO code of unit -> '{}' is not known - change `unit_iso_code` instead".format(unit)
            raise ValueError(message)

    return payload

    def to_odata(self) -> dict:
    """Return the OData payload of the purchase requisition - the units of its items only as ISO codes.

    Returns:
        dict:
            The payload with OData property names.

    """

    payload = super().to_odata()
    for item in payload.get("_PurchaseRequisitionItem", []):
        send_purchase_requisition_units_as_iso(item)

    return payload

    SAPRequestForQuotationAction ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Status actions for requests for quotation (function imports of API_RFQ_PROCESS_SRV).

    Lifecycle statuses: 01 in preparation, 06 in approval, 02 published, 05 completed, 03 cancelled, 07 rejected. The API has no separate publish action. Values (SAP function names) and their effect on the RFQ: * SubmitForApproval: only in preparation - starts SAP's approval workflow (in approval); the workflow publishes the RFQ to the bidders when it is approved or no approval is needed. Quotations need a published RFQ. * Complete: close a published RFQ (completed) - no more quotations. * Cancel: cancel the RFQ.

    SAPSupplierQuotationAction ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Status actions for supplier quotations (function imports of API_QTN_PROCESS_SRV).

    Lifecycle statuses: 01 in preparation, 02 submitted, 06 in approval, 03 awarded, 05 completed, 04 cancelled, 07 rejected. Values (SAP function names) and their effect on the quotation: * Submit: submit the quotation (the supplier's answer is final). * SubmitForApproval: award a submitted quotation - set the awarded quantities of its items first; SAP's approval workflow awards it when it is approved or no approval is needed. * Complete: close a submitted quotation without awarding it. * Cancel: cancel the quotation.

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_dates(self) -> Self:
    """Validate that the submission deadline is not before the earliest submission date."""

    if (
        self.submission_deadline
        and self.earliest_submission_date
        and self.submission_deadline < self.earliest_submission_date
    ):
        message = "Submission deadline -> {} is before the earliest submission date -> {}".format(
            self.submission_deadline,
            self.earliest_submission_date,
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_dates(self) -> Self:
    """Validate that the validity dates are given and the end date is not before the start date."""

    if not self.validity_start_date or not self.validity_end_date:
        message = "A source list record needs a validity start and end date"
        raise ValueError(message)
    if self.validity_end_date < self.validity_start_date:
        message = "Validity end date -> {} is before validity start date -> {}".format(
            self.validity_end_date,
            self.validity_start_date,
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_item_storage_location(self) -> Self:
    """Reject a storage location on create - $metadata: StorageLocation is not creatable (SAP determines it).

    It can only be changed on an existing delivery item (update_outbound_delivery()).

    """

    if any(item.storage_location for item in self.items):
        message = (
            "The storage location of a delivery item can't be set on create - SAP determines it; change it "
            "with an update of the delivery afterwards"
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_quantity(self) -> Self:
    """Require the invoiced quantity - only subsequent debits / credits (price differences) have none.

    Verified in S/4HANA: SAP ignores the amount of a purchase order item without a quantity and
    rejects the invoice with M8/186 "Balance is not equal to zero".

    """

    if self.quantity is None and not self.is_subsequent_debit_credit:
        message = (
            "Purchase order item {} of purchase order {} needs the invoiced quantity "
            "(QuantityInPurchaseOrderUnit) - without it SAP ignores the amount".format(
                self.purchase_order_item, self.purchase_order
            )
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    SAPSupplierInvoiceModel ¶

    Bases: SAPODataCreateModel

    Data to create (post) an SAP supplier invoice (API_SUPPLIERINVOICE_PROCESS_SRV, OData V2).

    Logistics invoice verification: the invoice of a supplier, usually for purchase order items (purchase_order_items) and / or posted to G/L accounts (gl_account_items), materials (material_items) or fixed assets (asset_items). Instead of giving the items, purchase orders, delivery notes or service entry sheets can be selected - SAP then proposes their open items (only when the invoice is posted directly, not together with purchase_order_items). The invoice is posted directly or parked (status 'A') and posted later (SAP.post_supplier_invoice()). The invoice number and fiscal year are assigned by SAP.

    See: https://api.sap.com/api/API_SUPPLIERINVOICE_PROCESS_SRV/overview

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def fill_currency(self) -> Self:
    """Fill in the document currency of the items, account assignments and taxes.

    SAP rejects items without it ("Document currency is missing in item ...") although it is
    the currency of the invoice.

    """

    children = [
        *self.purchase_order_items,
        *(
            account_assignment
            for item in self.purchase_order_items
            for account_assignment in item.account_assignments
        ),
        *self.gl_account_items,
        *self.material_items,
        *self.asset_items,
        *self.taxes,
        *self.withholding_taxes,
    ]
    for child in children:
        child.currency = child.currency or self.currency

    return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def fill_debit_credit_code(self) -> Self:
    """Fill in the debit / credit code of the G/L account, material and asset items.

    SAP requires it (M8/375 "Fill in mandatory field 'DebitCreditCode'"): debit 'S' for an
    invoice, credit 'H' for a credit memo - unless the item gives its own.

    """

    for item in [*self.gl_account_items, *self.material_items, *self.asset_items]:
        item.debit_credit_code = item.debit_credit_code or ("H" if self.is_credit_memo else "S")

    return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_items(self) -> Self:
    """Validate that the invoice has items - or selects the documents SAP proposes the items from."""

    if not any(
        (
            self.purchase_order_items,
            self.gl_account_items,
            self.material_items,
            self.asset_items,
            self.selected_purchase_orders,
            self.selected_delivery_notes,
            self.selected_service_entry_sheets,
        )
    ):
        message = (
            "A supplier invoice needs items (purchase order, G/L account, material or asset items) or selected "
            "purchase orders, delivery notes or service entry sheets"
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_taxes(self) -> Self:
    """Validate that the tax is either calculated automatically or given as tax lines - not both.

    Verified in S/4HANA: SAP rejects tax lines together with automatic tax calculation (M8/738
    "Enter value in either field 'TaxIsCalculatedAutomatically' or field 'TaxAmount'") - also tax
    lines with a tax amount of 0.

    """

    if self.tax_is_calculated_automatically and self.taxes:
        message = (
            "Give either TaxIsCalculatedAutomatically = true or the tax lines (to_SupplierInvoiceTax) - SAP "
            "rejects both together (M8/738). With automatic tax calculation, SAP calculates the tax from the "
            "tax codes of the items - leave out the tax lines"
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_selected_documents(self) -> Self:
    """Validate the selected purchase orders, delivery notes and service entry sheets.

    Verified in S/4HANA: SAP rejects selected documents together with purchase order items
    (M8/742 "Table 'to_SuplrInvcItemPurOrdRef' must not be filled"), and a parked invoice with
    selected documents is saved without items - it can't be posted later (M8/063).

    """

    if not (self.selected_purchase_orders or self.selected_delivery_notes or self.selected_service_entry_sheets):
        return self

    if self.purchase_order_items:
        message = (
            "Give either purchase_order_items or selected purchase orders / delivery notes / service entry "
            "sheets - SAP rejects both together (M8/742)"
        )
        raise ValueError(message)
    if self.status == "A":
        message = (
            "A parked invoice (status 'A') gets no items from selected purchase orders / delivery notes / service "
            "entry sheets - give purchase_order_items (with the goods receipt as reference_document for "
            "goods-receipt-based invoice verification) or post the invoice directly"
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    SAPMaintenanceOrderAction ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Status actions for maintenance orders (function imports of API_MAINTENANCEORDER).

    Values (SAP function names) and their effect on the order: * ReleaseMaintenanceOrder: release the order for execution (status REL). * ScheduleMaintenanceOrder: schedule the order (calculate the operation dates). * SetMaintOrderToReadyForSchedg / ResetMaintOrderStsRdyForSchedg: set / reset "ready for scheduling". * SubmitMaintOrderForApproval: submit the order for approval. * ApproveMaintenanceOrder / RejectMaintenanceOrder: approve / reject a submitted order. * SetMaintOrderStatusToLocked / SetMaintOrderStatusToUnlocked: lock (LKD) / unlock the order. * SetMaintOrdToMainWorkComplete / ResetMaintOrdStsMainWorkCmplt: set / reset "main work completed". * SetMaintOrdToTechCompleted / ResetMaintOrdStsTechCompleted: complete technically (TECO) / undo it. * SetMaintOrderStatusToClosed / ResetMaintOrderStatusClosed: close (CLSD, business completion) / undo it. * SetMaintOrdStsToMrkdForDeltn / ResetMaintOrdStsMrkdForDeltn: set / reset the deletion flag (DLFL). * SetMaintOrderToDoNotExecute: mark the order as "do not execute" (it will not be carried out).

    Some actions accept optional parameters (e.g. "MaintOrderReferenceDateTime" or "AssignedMaintNotifIsToBeClosed") - pass them to change_maintenance_order_status(). SetMaintOrdStsToMrkdForDeltn accepts "AssgdMaintNotifIsToBeSetDel" (True also sets the deletion flag of the assigned maintenance notification - API_MAINTNOTIFICATION itself cannot delete notifications). SAP only accepts it for closed orders - use delete_maintenance_order() which closes the order first.

    SAPMaintenanceOrderOperationAction ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Status actions for maintenance order operations (function imports of API_MAINTENANCEORDER).

    Values (SAP function names) and their effect on the operation: * SetMaintOrderOpToDispatched: dispatch the operation (status DSPT) - it is planned for execution by its work center at its scheduled dates. * ResetMaintOrderOpStsDispatched: undo the dispatching.

    Operations are deleted with delete_maintenance_order_operation().

    SAPMaintenanceNotificationAction ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Status actions for maintenance notifications (actions of API_MAINTNOTIFICATION).

    Values (SAP function names) and their effect on the notification: * CompleteMaintNotification: complete the notification (status NOCO). * SetMaintNotifToInProcess: put the notification in process (status NOPR).

    API_MAINTNOTIFICATION has no action to delete a notification (and does not allow DELETE). A notification assigned to an order can get the deletion flag together with its order - see delete_maintenance_order().

    SAPMaintenancePlanAction ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Status / scheduling actions for maintenance plans (actions of API_MAINTENANCEPLAN).

    Values (SAP function names) and their effect on the plan: * StartMaintPlnSchedule: start scheduling - generates the maintenance calls from the scheduling start date. * RestartMaintPlnSchedule: restart scheduling with a new start date. * SetMaintPlanStatusToActive / SetMaintPlanStatusToInactive: activate / deactivate the plan (no calls if inactive). * SetMainPlanStsToMrkdForDeltn / ResetMaintPlanStsMrkdForDeltn: set / reset the deletion flag.

    SAPProductionOrderAction ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Status actions for production orders (function imports of API_PRODUCTION_ORDER_2_SRV).

    Values (SAP function names) and their effect on the order: * ReleaseOrder: release the order for production (status REL). * TechlyCmpltOrder: complete the order technically (status TECO) - no further production. * CloseOrder: close the order (status CLSD) - no further postings. * DeletionFlagOrder: set the deletion flag (status DLFL). * DeletionIndOrder: set the deletion indicator (status DLT) - the order can be archived. * DiscardOrder: discard (cancel) the order. * DeliveryCompletedOrder: set "delivery completed" (status DLV) - no further goods receipts expected. * OrderReleasedByMES: record that the order has been released by a Manufacturing Execution System.

    SAPCreditMemoRequestAction ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Approval actions for credit memo requests (function imports of API_CREDIT_MEMO_REQUEST_SRV).

    Values (SAP function names) and their effect: * releaseApprovalRequest: approve (release) a credit memo request that is in approval. * rejectApprovalRequest: reject a credit memo request that is in approval.

    SAPOutboundDeliveryAction ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Status actions for outbound deliveries (function imports of API_OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV).

    Values (SAP function names) and their effect on the delivery: * PickAllItems: pick all items (picking quantity = delivery quantity). * ConfirmPickingAllItems: confirm the picking of all items. * PostGoodsIssue: post the goods issue - reduces the stock, the delivery can be billed. * ReverseGoodsIssue: reverse the goods issue - needs the parameter "ActualGoodsMovementDate". * DeleteAllHandlingUnitsFromDelivery: unpack the delivery (delete all handling units).

    Item actions (e.g. "PickOneItem", "ConfirmPickingOneItem") are called the same way with the parameter "DeliveryDocumentItem" - see change_outbound_delivery_status().

    SAPInboundDeliveryAction ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Status actions for inbound deliveries (function imports of API_INBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV).

    Values (SAP function names) and their effect on the delivery: * PutawayAllItems: put away all items (putaway quantity = delivery quantity). * ConfirmPutawayAllItems: confirm the putaway of all items. * PostGoodsReceipt: post the goods receipt - increases the stock. * ReverseGoodsReceipt: reverse the goods receipt - needs the parameter "ActualGoodsMovementDate".

    Item actions (e.g. "PutawayOneItem", "ConfirmPutawayOneItem") are called the same way with the parameter "DeliveryDocumentItem" - see change_inbound_delivery_status().

    SAPGoodsMovementItemModel ¶

    Bases: SAPODataCreateModel

    An item of a goods movement (material document item, API_MATERIAL_DOCUMENT_SRV).

    The movement type defines the business transaction, e.g. 101 (goods receipt for a purchase order - with purchase order, item and reference document type "B"), 201 (goods issue to a cost center), 261 (goods issue to a production order), 311 (transfer posting between storage locations) or 412 with special stock "E" (transfer posting from the plant's own stock into the sales order stock of a make-to-order sales order item - 411 "E" moves it back; both need the receiving storage location, e.g. the same storage location).

    The item fields SAP accepts are not in $metadata (no sap:creatable annotations) - SAP checks them at runtime per movement type, see check_allowed_fields().

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_sales_order_stock(self) -> Self:
    """Validate that sales order stock (special stock 'E') is given with its sales order item.

    Transfer postings between own and sales order stock (411 / 412 'E') also need the
    receiving storage location - SAP rejects them without it
    ("[MM_IM_ODATA_API_MDOC/010] Property IssuingOrReceivingStorageLoc is mandatory").

    """

    if (self.special_stock_type or "").upper() != "E":
        return self
    if not (self.sales_order_stock and self.sales_order_stock_item):
        message = (
            "Sales order stock (`special_stock_type` 'E') needs `sales_order_stock` and `sales_order_stock_item`"
        )
        raise ValueError(message)
    if self.movement_type in ("411", "412") and not self.receiving_storage_location:
        message = "Movement type {} 'E' needs the `receiving_storage_location`".format(self.movement_type)
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    check_allowed_fields ¶

    check_allowed_fields() -> Self

    Apply the item field rules of API_MATERIAL_DOCUMENT_SRV before the item is posted.

    $metadata has no sap:creatable annotations for the item - SAP checks the fields at runtime (CL_MATERIAL_DOCUMENT_API->GET_RELEVANT_FIELDS / ITEM_CHECK_ALLOWED_FIELDS): a fixed set of always allowed fields, the field selection of the movement type (customizing MIGO_CUST_FIELDS) and fields that depend on the reference document type or on transfer movement types. The rules that do not depend on the customizing:

    • Purchase order and delivery properties need reference document type "B" - and "B" needs the purchase order and its item.
    • With a reference document ("B" purchase order, "F" production order) SAP takes the account assignment from the order and rejects the account assignment properties that are not in the field selection of the goods receipt (e.g. a cost center the LLM copied from the purchase order item) - they are dropped.
    • A goods receipt for an order is no transfer posting - receiving properties are rejected.

    Errors are raised before the user is asked to confirm the posting.

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_allowed_fields(self) -> Self:
    """Apply the item field rules of API_MATERIAL_DOCUMENT_SRV before the item is posted.

    $metadata has no sap:creatable annotations for the item - SAP checks the fields at
    runtime (CL_MATERIAL_DOCUMENT_API->GET_RELEVANT_FIELDS / ITEM_CHECK_ALLOWED_FIELDS):
    a fixed set of always allowed fields, the field selection of the movement type
    (customizing MIGO_CUST_FIELDS) and fields that depend on the reference document type
    or on transfer movement types. The rules that do not depend on the customizing:

    * Purchase order and delivery properties need reference document type "B" - and "B"
      needs the purchase order and its item.
    * With a reference document ("B" purchase order, "F" production order) SAP takes the
      account assignment from the order and rejects the account assignment properties
      that are not in the field selection of the goods receipt (e.g. a cost center the
      LLM copied from the purchase order item) - they are dropped.
    * A goods receipt for an order is no transfer posting - receiving properties are rejected.

    Errors are raised before the user is asked to confirm the posting.

    """

    properties = self.model_dump(by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)

    reference_document_type = (self.reference_document_type or "").upper()
    purchase_order_properties = [name for name in self.PURCHASE_ORDER_PROPERTIES if properties.get(name)]
    if purchase_order_properties and reference_document_type != "B":
        message = "{} need reference document type 'B' (GoodsMovementRefDocType)".format(purchase_order_properties)
        raise ValueError(message)
    if reference_document_type == "B" and not (self.purchase_order and self.purchase_order_item):
        message = "Reference document type 'B' needs `purchase_order` and `purchase_order_item`"
        raise ValueError(message)

    if reference_document_type not in ("B", "F"):
        return self

    receiving = [name for name in self.RECEIVING_PROPERTIES if properties.get(name)]
    if receiving:
        message = "A goods receipt for a purchase / production order is no transfer posting - remove {}".format(
            receiving
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    # SAP derives the account assignment from the order - drop the ones the caller copied from it:
    for name in self.CUSTOMIZED_ACCOUNT_ASSIGNMENT_PROPERTIES:
        field_name = next((key for key, field in type(self).model_fields.items() if field.alias == name), None)
        if field_name:
            setattr(self, field_name, None)

    return self

    def to_odata(self, odata_version: int) -> dict:
    """Return the OData query options - the reference document also with leading zeros.

    ReferenceDocument is a free text field without ALPHA conversion: the goods issue of an outbound
    delivery stores the delivery number with leading zeros ('0080000155'), so '80000155' alone finds
    nothing. The value as given is kept for delivery notes of suppliers.

    Args:
        odata_version (int):
            The OData version of the service (2 or 4).

    Returns:
        dict:
            The query options ($filter, $orderby, $expand).

    """

    params = super().to_odata(odata_version=odata_version)
    reference = (self.reference_document or "").strip()
    if reference:
        values = dict.fromkeys((reference, reference.zfill(10) if reference.isdigit() else reference))
        condition = " or ".join(
            "ReferenceDocument eq {}".format(odata_literal(value, odata_version=odata_version)) for value in values
        )
        condition = "({})".format(condition) if len(values) > 1 else condition
        params["$filter"] = "{} and {}".format(params["$filter"], condition) if "$filter" in params else condition

    return params

    """Return the OData query options - without the segments of quantity 0 unless include_zero is set.

    The segments without stock are filtered by SAP, so that the limit and the paging only count

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_item_categories(self) -> Self:
    """Fill in the plan category for the items and check that plan and items have the same category.

    SAP requires the category for each item and only assigns items of the plan's category.

    """

    if not self.items:
        return self

    self.category = self.category or next((item.category for item in self.items if item.category), None)
    if not self.category:
        message = "The maintenance plan needs a category, e.g. 'PM'"
        raise ValueError(message)
    for item in self.items:
        item.category = item.category or self.category
    categories = {self.category} | {item.category for item in self.items}
    if len(categories) > 1:
        message = "Maintenance plan and items must have the same category, got -> {}".format(sorted(categories))
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    def accepts(self, entity: BaseModel) -> bool:
    """Check the deletion flag (system status I0076) - SAP can't filter by the system status (HTTP 501).

    Args:
        entity (BaseModel):
            The maintenance plan read (SAPMaintenancePlanResponseModel).

    Returns:
        bool:
            True if the plan matches is_marked_for_deletion (or the criterion isn't set).

    """

    if self.is_marked_for_deletion is None:
        return True

    plan = cast("SAPMaintenancePlanResponseModel", entity)

    return ("I0076" in (plan.system_status or "").split()) == self.is_marked_for_deletion

    SAPTaskListModel ¶

    Bases: SAPODataCreateModel

    Data to create an SAP maintenance task list (API_MAINTENANCETASKLIST, OData V4).

    A task list describes the work (operations) of a maintenance task. It can be referenced by maintenance plan items and maintenance orders. There are three types: general task lists ('A', not bound to an object), equipment task lists ('E', need equipment) and functional location task lists ('T', need functional_location). The task list group is assigned by SAP unless it is given.

    A general task list with an assembly (a material, e.g. the construction type of equipment) applies to all equipment of this type. The materials of its operations (e.g. spare parts) are allocated via the plant maintenance BOM of the assembly - they can only be created together with the task list (not added later).

    See: https://api.sap.com/api/OP_API_MAINTENANCETASKLIST_0001/overview

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_technical_object(self) -> Self:
    """Validate that equipment and functional location task lists have their technical object."""

    if self.task_list_type == "E" and not self.equipment:
        message = "Equipment task lists (type 'E') need an equipment"
        raise ValueError(message)
    if self.task_list_type == "T" and not self.functional_location:
        message = "Functional location task lists (type 'T') need a functional location"
        raise ValueError(message)
    self.assign_operation_keys()

    # The materials are allocated via the BOM of the assembly - a general task list has no other object:
    if (
        self.task_list_type == "A"
        and not self.assembly
        and any(operation.materials for operation in self.operations)
    ):
        message = (
            "General task lists (type 'A') with materials in their operations need an assembly - the material "
            "whose plant maintenance BOM contains them"
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    def assign_operation_keys(self) -> None:
    """Set the task list type and operation number in operations with materials and their materials.

    SAP needs them to allocate the materials in the deep create of the task list.

    """

    for operation in self.operations:
        if not operation.materials:
            continue
        operation.task_list_type = self.task_list_type
        for material in operation.materials:
            material.task_list_type = self.task_list_type
            material.operation = operation.operation

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_dates(self) -> Self:
    """Validate the dates and default the MRP area to the MRP plant.

    Without an explicit MRP area SAP rejects the procurement category ("MRP area E has not
    been defined").

    """

    self.mrp_area = self.mrp_area or self.mrp_plant
    if not self.start_date and not self.end_date:
        message = "Give an `end_date` and/or a `start_date` - SAP schedules the planned order from them"
        raise ValueError(message)
    if self.start_date and self.end_date and self.end_date < self.start_date:
        message = "Planned end date -> {} is before planned start date -> {}".format(
            self.end_date,
            self.start_date,
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    Validate the planned dates and derive the scheduling type.

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_dates(self) -> Self:
    """Validate the planned dates and derive the scheduling type.

    SAP schedules forwards from the start date or backwards from the end date. Without a
    scheduling type it uses the default of the order type (e.g. backwards for PP01), which
    fails if only the start date is given ("CO/028 Backward scheduling (enter finish date)").

    """

    if not self.planned_start_date and not self.planned_end_date:
        message = "Give a `planned_end_date` (backward scheduling) or a `planned_start_date` (forward scheduling)"
        raise ValueError(message)
    if not self.scheduling_type:
        self.scheduling_type = "2" if self.planned_end_date else "1"
    if self.scheduling_type == "1" and not self.planned_start_date:
        message = "Forward scheduling (`scheduling_type` '1') needs a `planned_start_date`"
        raise ValueError(message)
    if self.scheduling_type == "2" and not self.planned_end_date:
        message = "Backward scheduling (`scheduling_type` '2') needs a `planned_end_date`"
        raise ValueError(message)
    if self.planned_start_date and self.planned_end_date and self.planned_end_date < self.planned_start_date:
        message = "Planned end date -> {} is before planned start date -> {}".format(
            self.planned_end_date,
            self.planned_start_date,
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    def assign_product_id(self, product_id: str | None) -> None:

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_product_ids(self) -> Self:
    """Fill in the product number for the descriptions, plants and valuations (needed with an external number)."""

    for child in [*self.descriptions, *self.plants, *self.valuations]:
        child.product_id = child.product_id or self.product_id
        if child.product_id != self.product_id:
            message = "The descriptions, plants and valuations must belong to product -> '{}', got -> '{}'".format(
                self.product_id, child.product_id
            )
            raise ValueError(message)
    for plant in self.plants:
        plant.assign_product_id(self.product_id)

    return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_batch_management(self) -> Self:
    """Set batch management on the product and its plants - SAP needs it on both levels."""

    if self.is_batch_managed is None and any(plant.is_batch_managed for plant in self.plants):
        self.is_batch_managed = True
    for plant in self.plants:
        if plant.is_batch_managed is None:
            plant.is_batch_managed = self.is_batch_managed

    return self

    @model_validator(mode="before")
@classmethod
def number_items(cls, data: object) -> object:
    """Assign the item numbers 0010, 0020, ... to the items without one (after the highest given number)."""

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return data

    key = "to_BillOfMaterialItem" if "to_BillOfMaterialItem" in data else "items"
    items = data.get(key)
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        return data

    def given_number(item: object) -> int | None:
        if isinstance(item, dict):
            number = item.get("BillOfMaterialItemNumber", item.get("item_number"))
        else:
            number = getattr(item, "item_number", None)
        return int(number) if number not in (None, "") and str(number).strip().isdigit() else None

    next_number = max((number for item in items if (number := given_number(item)) is not None), default=0)
    numbered = []
    for item in items:
        if isinstance(item, dict) and given_number(item) is None:
            next_number += 10
            item = {**item, "BillOfMaterialItemNumber": str(next_number)}
        numbered.append(item)

    return {**data, key: numbered}

    SAPBusinessPartnerModel ¶

    Bases: SAPODataCreateModel

    Data to create an SAP business partner - an organization (API_BUSINESS_PARTNER, OData V2).

    Addresses, roles and the supplier / customer data are created together with the business partner (deep insert). With a supplier or customer role SAP also creates the supplier / customer - its number can differ from the business partner number (depending on the customizing of the grouping). Typical roles:

    • FLVN00: supplier - general and company code data (enough for the manufacturer of a product)
    • FLVN01: supplier - purchasing data (in addition to FLVN00 to order from the supplier)
    • FLCU00: customer - general and company code data
    • FLCU01: customer - sales data (in addition to FLCU00 to sell to the customer)

    Business partners cannot be deleted with the API.

    See: https://api.sap.com/api/API_BUSINESS_PARTNER/overview

    @model_validator(mode="after")
def check_supplier_roles(self) -> Self:
    """Check that the supplier data comes with the supplier roles it needs (FLVN00 / FLVN01)."""

    if not self.supplier:

    roles = {role.role for role in self.roles}
    if "FLVN00" not in roles:

    if self.supplier.purchasing_organizations and "FLVN01" not in roles:
        message = "Purchasing organization data needs the business partner role FLVN01 (supplier - purchasing)"
        raise ValueError(message)

    return self

    def to_odata(self, odata_version: int) -> dict:
    """Return the OData query options - the identifications are always expanded (they hold the personnel number).

    Args:
        odata_version (int):
            The OData version of the service (2 or 4).

    Returns:
        dict:
            The query options ($filter, $orderby, $expand).

    """

    params = super().to_odata(odata_version=odata_version)
    params["$expand"] = self.EXPAND if self.expand_items else "to_BuPaIdentification"

    return params

    def to_odata_conditions(self, odata_version: int, navigation: str = "", exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> list[str]:
    """Return the conditions - and the name conditions: SAP searches case-sensitively, so the common spellings are searched.

    Args:
        odata_version (int):
            The OData version of the service (2 or 4).
        navigation (str, optional):
            The to-one navigation property to the entity of this query (see the base class).
        exclude (tuple[str, ...], optional):
            Fields to leave out (see the base class).

    Returns:
        list[str]:
            The conditions of the fields and on the first and last name.

    """

    conditions = super().to_odata_conditions(odata_version=odata_version, navigation=navigation, exclude=exclude)
    conditions += [
        ODataCondition(property_name, operator="contains").to_filter(
            value=text_search_variants(term), odata_version=odata_version
        )
        for property_name, term in (("LastName", self.last_name_contains), ("FirstName", self.first_name_contains))
        if term and term.strip()
    ]

    return conditions

    def parse_odata_datetime(value: str | datetime | None) -> str | datetime | None:
    """Convert an OData V2 JSON date ("/Date(<ms>[+|-<offset>])/") into a timezone-aware datetime.

    Used as a pydantic "before" validator (see ODataDateTime). Other values
    (datetime objects, ISO 8601 strings, None) are passed through unchanged
    and handled by pydantic's standard datetime parsing.

    The milliseconds are always counted from 1970-01-01 UTC. The optional offset
    is given in minutes (e.g. "+0120" = UTC+02:00) and only determines the timezone
    of the result, not the point in time. Values without offset (Edm.DateTime) are
    returned in UTC.

    Args:
        value (str | datetime | None):
            The value to convert, e.g. "/Date(1724354331000+0000)/".

    Returns:
        str | datetime | None:
            The timezone-aware datetime (e.g. 2024-08-22 19:18:51+00:00) for OData V2
            dates, None for initial (empty) OData V2 dates, otherwise the unchanged value.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            If the value looks like an OData V2 date but is malformed.

    """

    # Some services (e.g. API_PRODUCTION_ORDER_2_SRV) return an ABAP timestamp
    # (YYYYMMDDhhmmss in UTC, e.g. "20160412160912") - pydantic would read it as
    # milliseconds since 1970. An initial timestamp ("00000000000000") means no value:
    if isinstance(value, str) and len(value) == 14 and value.isdigit():
        return None if int(value) == 0 else datetime.strptime(value, "%Y%m%d%H%M%S").replace(tzinfo=UTC)

    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.startswith("/Date("):
        return value

    match = ODATA_V2_DATE_PATTERN.match(value)
    if not match:
        message = "Invalid OData V2 date value -> '{}'".format(value)
        raise ValueError(message)

    milliseconds, offset_minutes = match.groups()
    if int(milliseconds) < ODATA_V2_MIN_MILLISECONDS:
        return None
    result = datetime.fromtimestamp(int(milliseconds) / 1000, tz=UTC)
    if offset_minutes:
        result = result.astimezone(timezone(timedelta(minutes=int(offset_minutes))))

    return result

    def serialize_odata_datetime(value: datetime | None) -> str | None:
    """Serialize a datetime in the OData V2 JSON format for Edm.DateTimeOffset ("/Date(<ms>+0000)/").

    Args:
        value (datetime | None):
            The datetime to serialize. Datetimes without timezone are treated as UTC.

    Returns:
        str | None:
            The OData V2 JSON datetime (in UTC) or None.

    """

    if value is None:
        return None
    if value.tzinfo is None:
        value = value.replace(tzinfo=UTC)

    return "/Date({}+0000)/".format(int(value.timestamp() * 1000))

    def parse_odata_date(value: str | date | None) -> str | date | None:
    """Convert an OData V2 JSON date ("/Date(<ms of midnight UTC>)/") into a date.

    Used as a pydantic "before" validator (see ODataDate) for Edm.DateTime
    properties with date semantics. Other values (date objects, ISO 8601
    strings, None) are passed through unchanged.

    Args:

            The value to convert, e.g. "/Date(1791504000000)/".

    Returns:
        str | date | None:
            The date for OData V2 dates, otherwise the unchanged value.

    """

    parsed = parse_odata_datetime(value) if isinstance(value, str) else value

    return parsed.date() if isinstance(parsed, datetime) else parsed

    def parse_odata_time(value: str | dtime | None) -> str | dtime | None:
    """Convert an OData V2 JSON time (Edm.Time, e.g. "PT08H30M00S") into a time.

    Other values (time objects, ISO 8601 strings like "08:30", None) are passed
    through unchanged and handled by pydantic's standard time parsing.

    Args:
        value (str | dtime | None):
            The value to convert.

    Returns:
        str | dtime | None:
            The time for OData V2 times, otherwise the unchanged value.

    """

    match = ODATA_V2_TIME_PATTERN.match(value) if isinstance(value, str) else None
    if not match:
        return value
    hours, minutes, seconds = (int(part) for part in match.groups())
    # SAP uses "PT24H00M00S" for the end of the day - a time cannot hold 24:00:00:
    if (hours, minutes, seconds) == (24, 0, 0):
        return dtime(23, 59, 59)

    return dtime(hours, minutes, seconds)

    def unwrap_odata_navigation(value: dict | list | None) -> list | None:
    """Unwrap the OData V2 representation of a to-many navigation property.

    Used as a pydantic "before" validator. SAP returns {"__deferred": {"uri": ...}}
    if the navigation property was not expanded and {"results": [...]} if it was
    expanded with $expand. OData V4 returns plain lists (or omits the property if
    not expanded), which are passed through.

    Args:
        value (dict | list | None):
            The raw value of the navigation property.

    Returns:
        list | None:
            The list of child entities or None if they have not been expanded.

    """

    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if "__deferred" in value:
            return None
        return value.get("results", [])

    return value

    def pad_number(value: str | int, length: int) -> str:
    """Normalize an SAP item / sequence number (NUMC) to its fixed length (e.g. 10 -> '00010').

    Args:
        value (str | int):
            The number, e.g. 10 or "10".
        length (int):
            The fixed length of the SAP field, e.g. 5 for purchase order items.

    Returns:
        str:
            The number padded with leading zeros.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            If the value is not numeric or too long.

    """

    value = str(value).strip()
    if not value.isdigit() or len(value) > length:
        message = "Must be numeric with up to {} digits, got -> '{}'".format(length, value)
        raise ValueError(message)

    return value.zfill(length)
